newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban renews amnesty offer to ousted leaders.
newsitem.headline: Taleban renews amnesty offer to ousted leaders.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic movement, which captured the capital Kabul on Friday, renewed on Sunday an offer of amnesty for the ousted government's leaders.
But a statement by Taleban's supreme leader Mullah Mohammad Omar, quoted by a Pakistan-based private Afghan news service, made the amnesty conditional on a return of state assets.

Taleban sources, quoted by the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), said the offer was aimed at ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, his prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, military commander Ahmad Shah Masood, and their ally, Abdurrab Rasul Sayyaf, leader of the Ittehad-i-Islami party.

Omar's statement, issued from Taleban headquarters in the southern Afghan town of Kandahar, asked them in the national interest to return all military and non-military assets they held to the public treasury immediately.
"After that the government will be prepared to talk to you," he said, urging them to take advantage of the general amnesty offered earlier.
Omar added that he was sorry to see them engaging in what he regarded as undesirable activities after being leaders of the jihad (holy war) against Soviet occupation in the 1980s.
State-run Radio Pakistan earlier quoted the leader of Taleban's new administration in Kabul as ruling out any role for Rabbani, Hekmatyar and Masood in the future government.
